category_title: Students without academic skill deficits who engage in active/disruptive work avoidance
student_description: Martin is a capable second-grade student who frequently engages in off-task and disruptive behaviors, such as leaving his seat and talking to peers, primarily to avoid instructional tasks. Because his behavior is maintained by work avoidance rather than a need for attention or academic remediation, he uniquely requires structured, appropriate ways to take breaks and frequent, point-based feedback tied to tangible incentives to make academic engagement more rewarding.

criteria.rationale: Martin's disruptive behavior is driven by work avoidance, so providing a sanctioned, time-limited break fulfills this need appropriately without causing classroom disruption.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts the student to use a break card or explicitly offers a structured, time-limited break option (e.g., resting, doodling, coloring) when work avoidance behaviors occur.

criteria.rationale: Simply telling Martin to stop talking is ineffective; he needs immediate, explicit instruction on the correct replacement behavior to understand expectations.
criteria.check: The tutor provides explicit, instructional feedback on what the student should do (e.g., how to request a break or how to engage with the task) rather than solely issuing a reprimand or telling him what not to do.
